why: Type parameters everywhere: a generic interface, a generic class implementing it at the same parameter, a generic method, and a generic free function. The question is whether the parameter list changes the identity of what is emitted — a node id carrying `<T>`, or an IMPLEMENTS edge lost because the interface is written `Repo<T>` at the implements site rather than `Repo`.
excluded: `this.items.get(id)` — a method call on a class property, which needs the property's type. The front-end documents instance calls on a typed variable as skipped; `instance_calls` is the case that measures that directly.
`new Map()` — construction of a built-in with no node in the scanned tree.

**Resolved (was an open question).** Generic type parameters are stripped from node ids: `ts:app/repo.Repo`, not `ts:app/repo.Repo<T>`. The id scheme is `{module}.{name}` and a type parameter is not part of the declared name. The case scores as labelled, which is the observation that settles it.
